note_on_method: Each venue page rests on one Town of Mount Pleasant page - the Recreation Department's pickleball page, which lists every venue under an Indoor or Outdoor heading with a count, a two-line address and a paragraph of rules - plus the US Census address geocoder for the county and the postcode. Park West is two Town entries at one address, published as one venue. Where the Town is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
One indoor pickleball court at the Town's Senior Center on Von Kolnitz Road, listed on the Town's pickleball page as "Mount Pleasant Senior Center 50+ / 1 Court". The "50+" is not part of the building's name; it is the condition of entry, and the Town spells it out beneath: "Drop-in play is for anyone 50 years and older and is free for members of the Senior Center."

The paragraph that follows is unusually complete for a single court. Non-members "may join in for a guest fee of $5 for Mt. Pleasant residents and $10 for those residing outside of Mt. Pleasant", and "Nets, balls, and paddles are provided" - the one venue in Mount Pleasant where you can arrive with nothing in your hands. Sessions are Tuesday and Thursday 3:00 to 4:50 pm and Friday 3:00 to 5:50 pm, with "101 Lessons with Al" on Fridays from 1:00 to 2:50 pm beforehand. The Town gives a phone number for the centre, 843-856-2166, and says nothing about the building beyond that.

One court is one game at a time: four players on and everyone else waiting.
slots.getting_there:
840 Von Kolnitz Road, Mount Pleasant, SC 29464, as the Town prints it. The US Census address geocoder matched "840 VON KOLNITZ RD, MOUNT PLEASANT, SC, 29464" at house-number level, placed it in Charleston County and in the incorporated place Mount Pleasant town, which is what lets it publish under Mount Pleasant, and the postcodes agree.

The Town publishes nothing about parking, transit or restrooms at the Senior Center, and nothing on this page about the building's own opening hours; the times above are pickleball sessions. Non-members should expect to pay the guest fee on arrival, since the Town states it as the condition of joining in.
slots.what_to_expect:
A drop-in for players 50 and older, on one court, three afternoons a week. Members of the Senior Center play free; anyone else pays $5 as a Mount Pleasant resident or $10 from outside the town, in the Town's own figures. That is why this venue publishes with a drop-in fee rather than as free: free for a member is not free for the public.

Equipment is the thing to notice. Everywhere else in Mount Pleasant the Town lends a net and asks you to bring paddles and balls; here it provides all three. The Town also prints a line reading "MTWTFS: 6:00 am" under the entry without saying what it refers to, so it is not read here as a pickleball session.

With one court there is no rotation to speak of, and the Town says nothing about how many people come. Surface is not stated, and lighting inside a gym is not something the Town addresses. The Friday lesson hour, 1:00 to 2:50 pm, runs before the Friday session rather than during it.

faqs.a: One, listed under the Town's Indoor heading as "Mount Pleasant Senior Center 50+ / 1 Court".
Anyone 50 years and older, in the Town's words. It is the one Mount Pleasant venue with an age condition.
For members of the Senior Center, yes. Non-members pay a guest fee of $5 if they live in Mount Pleasant and $10 if they do not.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring anything?
faqs.a: No. "Nets, balls, and paddles are provided", which the Town states at no other Mount Pleasant venue.
Tuesday and Thursday 3:00 to 4:50 pm and Friday 3:00 to 5:50 pm, with "101 Lessons with Al" on Fridays 1:00 to 2:50 pm.

slots.description:
Ten pickleball courts at one address in the Park West complex, on both sides of the indoor line: six in the Park West Gym and four lit courts on the Park West Tennis Courts. The Town lists them as two entries on its pickleball page - "Park West Gym / 6 Courts" under Indoor and "Park West Tennis Courts / 4 Courts - Lighted" under Outdoor - both at 1251 Park West Boulevard, and they publish here as one venue. Ten is the sum of the Town's two figures.

The six is stated twice. Besides the Indoor entry, the Town's notice for the Al Bradshaw-Whittemore Pickleball Classic, held here on April 18 and 19, 2026, gives the location as "Park West Gym / 6 Indoor Courts". The four outside are tennis courts first, in name and in the Town's own warning: "Our MPRD Tennis Pros do have court priority for lessons!" A Program Building stands "directly beside the courts" and is where the nets are kept.

This is a minted venue: no imported row carried both halves, and the imported row for the gym alone is left pending rather than published as a second venue at the same address.
slots.getting_there:
1251 Park West Boulevard, Mount Pleasant, SC 29466, the address the Town prints under both entries. The US Census address geocoder matched "1251 PARK WEST BLVD, MOUNT PLEASANT, SC, 29466" at house-number level, in Charleston County, in the incorporated place Mount Pleasant town, and the postcodes agree.

The Town publishes nothing about parking, transit or restrooms here. It does say where to go once you arrive: sign in at the gym, where "All players MUST sign in", and collect a net from the Program Building beside the outdoor courts, Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The gym is closed to pickleball for voting on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and on Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve.
slots.what_to_expect:
Two different days at one address. Indoors, six courts on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, 8:00 am to 12:00 pm, and on eight listed Sunday mornings from September 13 to November 15, 2026. "Drop-in play is free", nets are provided for players to set up, only water is allowed in the gym, and the Town asks players to "enter at their designated time and prepare for breakdown a few minutes prior to end time". Bring your own balls and paddles.

Outdoors, four lit tennis courts, "first come first served and free". Nets come from the Program Building on weekdays until 5:00 p.m., and "You must provide your own net if playing outside of business hours." The Town's tennis pros have priority for lessons, and Monday afternoons from 3:30 to 6:30 pm are closed to pickleball from August 24 to December 7, 2026, with September 7 excepted. An open play group meets Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday from 6:00 to 8:00 pm, reserved through the TeamReach app with the code 29466, and the Town's closure list reserves Mondays 6:30 to 8:30 pm for group play, half an hour later than the group's own line. Surface is not stated.

faqs.a: Ten: six in the Park West Gym, under the Town's Indoor heading, and four on the Park West Tennis Courts, under Outdoor, at the same address.
The four outdoor tennis courts are - "4 Courts - Lighted" is the Town's line. The six gym courts are indoors and the Town says nothing about lighting there.
Yes, on both sides: "Drop-in play is free" in the gym and "first come first served and free" on the tennis courts.
Not indoors, where nets are provided. Outdoors the Program Building lends them Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; outside business hours you must bring your own.

faqs.q: How do I join the evening group?
faqs.a: Reserve a spot on the TeamReach app with the code 29466. The group meets on the tennis courts Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, 6:00 to 8:00 pm.

slots.description:
Four indoor pickleball courts in the gym at the Town's Municipal Complex on Ann Edwards Lane, listed on the Town's pickleball page as "The Deb Gym at Town Hall / 4 Courts" under its Indoor heading. Town Hall is the Town's own address, the Municipal Complex at 100 Ann Edwards Lane.

The Town's paragraph is the same one it prints for Park West Gym: "Drop-in play is free. All players MUST sign in. Only water allowed inside the gym. NO OTHER FOOD OR DRINK ALLOWED." Nets are provided for players to set up; balls and paddles are yours to bring. What is particular to this gym is the season. "During volleyball season - Friday, September 18th through Saturday, October 31st all Pickleball Open Gyms will only be played on two pickleball courts." Four is the count the Town states and two is what to expect for six weeks of the autumn.

This is also where the Town runs its instructional clinics and private lessons with Kekoa Lee, for ages 18 and up, eight players a clinic. Those carry lesson prices, not court prices. This is a minted venue; no imported row carried it.
slots.getting_there:
100 Ann Edwards Lane, Mount Pleasant, SC 29464. The Town's pickleball page prints the street as "Ann Edwards Lane" under the venue entry and "Anne Edwards Lane" in its clinic section a few lines above; the Town's own footer uses Ann, and the US Census address geocoder matched "100 ANN EDWARDS LN, MOUNT PLEASANT, SC, 29464" at house-number level, in Charleston County, in the incorporated place Mount Pleasant town. Ann is what publishes.

The Town publishes nothing about parking, transit or restrooms at Town Hall on this page. You sign in on arrival, and only water goes into the gym with you.
slots.what_to_expect:
Three weekday sessions, all free, all in daylight hours: Mondays 1:00 to 3:00 pm, Wednesdays 9:00 am to 12:00 pm and Fridays 8:00 am to 12:00 pm. Four courts is two games at once, or a group of eight rotating without a long wait, in the weeks when all four are up.

Check the date before you go. Between September 18 and October 31 the floor is shared with volleyball season and the Town says plainly that open gym "will only be played on two pickleball courts". The Town also lists the days the gym is closed to pickleball: Labor Day, September 7; a Town wellness fair on Wednesday, September 16; Veterans Day, November 11; the day after Thanksgiving, November 27; and Christmas Day.

Enter at the designated time, sign in, and be ready to break the nets down a few minutes before the end - those are the Town's instructions for its gyms. Bring balls and paddles. The Town says nothing about surface, about how busy the sessions are, or about lighting, which in a gym is not a question it addresses.

faqs.a: Four, in the Town's words "The Deb Gym at Town Hall / 4 Courts" - reduced to two during volleyball season, September 18 to October 31.
Yes. "Drop-in play is free", in the Town's words, with a sign-in at the door and only water allowed inside the gym.
Mondays 1:00 to 3:00 pm, Wednesdays 9:00 am to 12:00 pm and Fridays 8:00 am to 12:00 pm, apart from the closure dates the Town lists.
Yes, for players to set up. Bring your own balls and paddles; only water is allowed inside the gym.

faqs.q: Is it Ann or Anne Edwards Lane?
faqs.a: The Town's page uses both spellings. The venue entry, the Town's footer and the Census address file all say Ann, and that is what publishes.

slots.description:
Four outdoor pickleball courts at the Miriam Brown Community Center on Royall Avenue, listed under the Town's Outdoor heading as "Miriam Brown Community Center / 4 Courts". They are free and "first come, first served", in the Town's words, with nets lent on weekdays from the G.M. Darby Building, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and paddles and balls to bring yourself.

The rule that shapes the day is printed in capitals: "NO OPEN PICKLEBALL PLAY WHEN THE COMMUNITY CENTER IS OPEN!" The Town then defines when that is - Monday to Friday 2:30 to 6:30 pm and Saturday 11:00 am to 3:30 pm from September to May, Monday to Friday 11:30 am to 3:30 pm from June to August - which is the most exact statement of when not to play at any of Mount Pleasant's four venues.

This is also where the Town's outdoor clinics run, under Coach Don Fickling, "a PCI Certified Pickleball Coach", assisted by Jackie Kelly, "USA Pickleball Ambassador", who together "lead Old Blue Truck Pickleball". The Town says nothing about what the courts are drawn on and nothing about lights.
slots.getting_there:
118 Royall Avenue, Mount Pleasant, SC 29464, as the Town prints it - Royall with two Ls, which corrected an imported row that had it as Royal Ave. The US Census address geocoder matched "118 ROYALL AVE, MOUNT PLEASANT, SC, 29464" at house-number level, in Charleston County, in the incorporated place Mount Pleasant town, and the postcodes agree.

The Town publishes nothing about parking, transit or restrooms here. The one building it names is the G.M. Darby Building, where the nets are kept on weekdays, and it does not say how far that is from the courts. Outside 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., or at the weekend, bring a net.
slots.what_to_expect:
A morning venue by habit and an afternoon closure by rule. The Town's open play group "Meets Monday - Sunday: 7:00am - 11:00 am", every day of the week, which is the only daily session in Mount Pleasant and the one that makes turning up alone a reasonable plan. Four courts is two games at once.

Then the ban. From September to May there is no open pickleball on weekday afternoons and early evenings, 2:30 to 6:30 pm, or on Saturdays from 11:00 am to 3:30 pm; from June to August the weekday closure runs 11:30 am to 3:30 pm instead. The Town adds that "Times may vary to accommodate MPRD activities."

Nets come from the G.M. Darby Building on weekdays only, so a Saturday or Sunday morning means your own net. Lighting is not stated, and with the daily group ending at 11:00 am nothing the Town prints depends on it. Surface is not stated. Clinics and private lessons with Coach Fickling are offered here at published prices, for ages 18 and up; those are lesson prices, and the price of the courts is nothing.

faqs.a: Four, outdoors, under the Town's Outdoor heading: "Miriam Brown Community Center / 4 Courts". Four courts is two games at once.
Yes: "Drop-in play is free and first come, first served." The clinics the Town runs here carry prices, but those are lesson prices.

Whenever the community centre is open, in the Town's capitals. September to May that is Monday to Friday 2:30 to 6:30 pm and Saturday 11:00 am to 3:30 pm; June to August, Monday to Friday 11:30 am to 3:30 pm.
Lent on weekdays from the G.M. Darby Building, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Bring your own at weekends, and bring paddles and balls always.
Not stated. The Town marks lighting at the Park West tennis courts and says nothing here, so it is recorded as unverified rather than as a no.
